## Advance several blocks in one process (`distribute.blocks_per_process`) {#sec-ch01-mesh}

### Summary

A `Mesh` holds several blocks in one process. It clones the block options for each, gives each block its own piece of
the grid, and advances them through a small worker pool. On a CUDA device every worker has its own stream. The mesh
also does once per step what each block would otherwise do alone: the time-step reduction, the redo decision and the
gravity-work fixer.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** N/A, a code map: clone and repartition the options, advance the local blocks, then exchange.

**Data.** In: one options tree and `blocks_per_process`[^rg-8de7fd51747b]. Out: the local blocks, each with its own variable map.

**Placement.** The mesh advances all local blocks, then exchanges, once per stage.

**Activation.** YAML `distribute.blocks_per_process` (default 1); the pool serves more than one block.

**Guarantee / limits.** A map; no convergence order. An $x_1$ anchor wait fails after five minutes.

**Evidence.** `test_mesh_multi_block.<b>` (two ranks, `allclose`), `test_mesh_exchange_python` (exact); see Tests.
:::

Local symbols: $n_b$ is the number of local blocks of a rank, $n_p$ the number of ranks and $n_{\mathrm{cell}}$ the
interior cells of a block. $a_{kj}$ is the contribution of cell $j$ to block term $b_k$ of the fixer sum.
$\delta_{\mathrm{mach}} = 2^{-53}$ is the unit round-off in double precision.

### Derivation

No separate derivation: this section describes an interface or control-flow path, and the operators are derived
in their owning chapters.

### Numerical method

`MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}) reads
`distribute.blocks_per_process` with the default 1. `MeshImpl::reset` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}})
requires it positive, clones the block options once per local block and repartitions each clone's coordinates through
its layout. The worker pool `BlockWorkerPool` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::BlockWorkerPool >}}) runs one
thread per block. On a CUDA device it takes one stream per block from the pool. It records the caller's stream in an
event every worker waits on, and records a done event per worker that the caller's stream waits on. The blocks'
kernels thus run on their own streams. `MeshImpl::max_time_step`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}) takes the minimum of the local bounds, then one MIN over the
process group, then the Courant factor and the redo halving. `MeshImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}) advances every local block with the fixer deferred. On the last
stage it sums the fixer terms of the local blocks, reduces them once with SUM, applies the common correction and
refills the physical boundaries. It then exchanges the ghosts of every block. `MeshImpl::check_redo`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}) combines the blocks' local flags on the device (one
device-to-host read when they share a device) before the one reduction. Stream assignment is an execution policy, not
evidence of numerical equivalence between decompositions.

```{python}

#| fig-alt: "Sequence: caller event; per-block workers; advance / local budgets; global fixer; exchange / joined events."
#| echo: false

make_fig()
```

**Why the mesh reduces once.** Three facts of the code, with the round-off of the one sum bounded in step 3.

1. The time step is the minimum of the local bounds, then one MIN over the process group
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}); a minimum selects an operand and adds no round-off.
2. The redo decision combines the blocks' flags on the device and crosses the process group once
   ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}); a flag is 0 or 1, so the combination is exact.
3. The gravity-work fixer sums five terms per block over the $n_b$ local blocks, then once over the $n_p$ ranks
   with SUM ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}). Each block term $b_k$ is itself a sum of
   $n_{\mathrm{cell}}$ cell contributions $a_{kj}$ (@sec-ch06-fixer). A sum of $n$ doubles accumulated in sequence
   has an error of at most $(n-1)\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}$ times the sum of the terms' magnitudes. The per-block
   sums therefore contribute at most $(n_{\mathrm{cell}}-1)\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\sum_{k,j}|a_{kj}|$, and the
   combination of the $n_b n_p$ block terms at most $(n_b n_p - 1)\,\delta_{\mathrm{mach}}\sum_k|b_k|$. A different
   block count therefore changes the common correction by round-off only.

: Implementation anchors for the mesh. {#tbl-ch01-mesh-code}

1. Read the block count and build the clones: `from_yaml` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}),
   `reset` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}}).
2. Advance the blocks through the pool and reduce once: `forward` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}),
   `max_time_step` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}),
   `check_redo` ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}).
3. Message tags and the $x_1$ anchor wait: `send_to_block` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::send_to_block >}}),
   `take_x1_anchor` ({{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutImpl::take_x1_anchor >}}).

**How to use it.** The `distribute`[^rg-8f3010cdaece] block names the layout and the local block count:

<!-- reader glossary keys -->Keys in this fragment: `layout`[^rg-b7bb60acd6d2], `nb1`[^rg-55fe49bed3ce], `nb2`[^rg-cbf2d5a13e1b], `nb3`[^rg-a3366ec76446].
```yaml
distribute:
  layout: slab          # or cubed, cubed-sphere
  nb1: 1
  nb2: 2
  nb3: 1
  blocks_per_process: 2 # local blocks; default 1
```

Refused: a key other than `layout`, `nb1`, `nb2`, `nb3`, `verbose`, `blocks_per_process` and `backend`, and a
non-positive `blocks_per_process`; `backend` is accepted and ignored, the environment `BACKEND` wins
(@sec-ch12-layout). The mesh order of a stage is these lines of `MeshImpl::forward`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}):

```cpp
if (blocks.size() == 1) {
  blocks[0]->advance_local(vars[0], dt, stage);
  blocks[0]->exchange_ghost_zones(vars[0]);
  return;
}
for (auto& b : blocks) b->defer_gravity_work_fixer = true;
run_block_jobs(
    [&](size_t i) { blocks[i]->advance_local(vars[i], dt, stage); });
// ... last stage: sum the fixer terms, one SUM, apply, refill the physical boundaries ...
run_block_jobs([&](size_t i) { blocks[i]->exchange_ghost_zones(vars[i]); });
```

The first block is the one-block fast path; the deferral line and the two `run_block_jobs` calls are steps 2
and 3 of the walk-through.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
A driver-split source applied after a mesh call makes the exchanged ghosts stale before the next advance; this
follows from the call order and is not a measured drift. Remote message tags allow at most 16 blocks per
process. The local $x_1$ anchor wait needs a producer that runs concurrently or earlier and fails after its
five-minute timeout.
:::
